items: How to Join as a Member

slides.text: The Linux Foundation's **goal is to create the greatest shared technology investment in history** by enabling open collaboration across companies, developers and users.
slides.sub: We are the nonprofit organization of choice to build ecosystems that accelerate open source technology development and commercial adoption on a global scale.

slides.title: We are behind some of the most critical projects in the world
Successful open collaboration ecosystems come down to four core factors.

cards.heading: Neutrality
cards.text: No one company or organization can “take it away” from the community that forms around a project.

cards.heading: IP Clarity
cards.text: Removal of Intellectual Property uncertainty enables anyone to get involved as a contributor or implement as a user.

cards.heading: Open Governance Do-ocracy
cards.text: The most successful projects that have stood the test of time have neutral, open governance models where those who do the work make the decisions in a defined governance model.

cards.heading: Financial Support Ecosystem
cards.text: Encouraging academic, government, and commercial engagement leads to jobs, faster adoption, new contributions and features that address new use cases.

left.heading: The x402 Foundation
bullets: **Stewards** supporting the open development of the x402 standard
**Drives** development, open governance, and widespread adoption

right.heading: The x402 Standard
bullets: **Extensible across internet payment networks**, including stablecoins, cards, and other rails
**Established** in 2026 as x402 a Series of LF Projects, LLC

slides.vision: The x402 Foundation champions open, neutral, agentic commerce.
slides.mission: x402 is a neutral open standard enabling direct, programmable internet payments, seamlessly integrating value transfer into web infrastructure and empowering developers, businesses, and users in a fairer digital economy.
strategy: Develop and grow adoption of the x402 standard
Research, develop, and form industry consensus of complementary standards for concepts such as identity, reputation, and discovery
Develop global ecosystem to ensure the agentic web is open to all, through events, education, development grants, and more

slides.title: The Current State: every API call and every AI agent still has a human-shaped payment flow

rows.label: No account, no access
rows.text: Clients that can sign a request still can't pay for one without creating an account, entering a card, and clearing KYC first — a workflow built for people, not software.

rows.label: Sub-dollar charges don't clear
rows.text: Per-transaction and percentage-based processor fees make pay-per-call, pay-per-query, and pay-per-inference pricing uneconomic below a few dollars.

rows.label: One-off payment integrations per vendor
rows.text: Every new chain, wallet, or facilitator today means another bespoke integration — many separate chain packages exist because there is no shared interface.

slides.footnote: For example: Stripe/Tempo's Machine Payments Protocol, Google's Agent Payments Protocol, and proprietary card-network schemes — without a shared layer, agentic commerce fragments before it scales

slides.title: One request, one response, paid.  Supporting a broad array of commerce.

steps.heading: Client requests
steps.text: A client calls a resource server for an API, dataset, content, or other goods and services.

steps.heading: 402 returned
steps.text: The server replies “402 Payment Required” with accepted payment options — no separate account or checkout flow.

steps.heading: Client pays & retries
steps.text: The client signs a payment payload for the network it prefers, and resends the request.

steps.heading: Verified & settled
steps.text: A facilitator verifies and settles the payment; the resource server returns 200 OK with the resource.

slides.title: Designed for composability: seamless integration without vendor lock-in

cards.heading: Focused scope
cards.text: x402 is strictly focused on supporting payment-specific communication between actors.

cards.heading: MCP & A2A Protocols
cards.text: Already integrated with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) frameworks for native, autonomous transaction handling.

cards.heading: UCP & AP2 Alignment
cards.text: Works in tandem with Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), passing delegated authority signals smoothly across layers.

slides.title: Welcome, Michael Hursta!
slides.heading: Michael joins the x402 Foundation as Executive Director.
slides.text: With over two decades in payments leadership, his full-stack view of the ecosystem – spanning issuers, processors, and platforms – prepares him to help align x402's members around one open standard.

slides.title: What members get that users don't

cards.heading: Influence
cards.text: Be at the center of the movement reshaping the payments ecosystem. A governing board seat (Premier) or elected representation (General) over budget, roadmap, and the specs that will run through your infrastructure.

cards.heading: Access
cards.text: A direct line to the TSC (Technical Steering Committee) and working groups shaping use case and new network support — before they ship.

cards.heading: Visibility
cards.text: Placement alongside Visa, Mastercard, AWS, Google, Stripe, and Coinbase in the member showcase, spotlights and blogs on x402.org.

cards.heading: De-risking
cards.text: Neutral Linux Foundation governance and global ecosystem-wide development and adoption de-risks your adoption of and dependency on the protocol and associated technology stack.

slides.title: What's next — and where members hold the pen

cards.heading: Card Acceptance working group
cards.text: Extending scheme support so card-funded flows can settle through x402 alongside stablecoins.

cards.heading: Identity working group
cards.text: Defining how much identity a payment needs to carry — balancing accountless access with compliance.

cards.heading: Tax working group
cards.text: Working through tax-reporting implications of high-frequency, low-value machine payments.

cards.heading: Scheme & network extensions
cards.text: New schemes (beyond exact, upto, and batch-settlement) and new network support move through public CONTRIBUTING.md acceptance criteria — member engineers can propose and ship them.

callout.heading: Your priority here — this box is intentionally blank
callout.text: Have a technical area you care about that isn't on this list? Bring it! New working groups are chartered through the Technical Steering Committee (TSC) where every Participating Org holds a seat.

slides.title: Membership ROI by Role
rows: Architecture risk from betting on a single vendor's payment rail
A Governing or General Board voice in the spec before it's locked in; no vendor lock-in
Early access to scheme extensions (e.g. Card Acceptance) before general release, plus press & showcase visibility
Bespoke integration work for every network and facilitator
A seat in the working groups defining shared SDKs and facilitator standards; less to build in-house
Direct input into the Identity and Tax working groups shaping how compliance is handled at the standard level

slides.title: Sign, onboard, ship — inside your first 90 days

steps.heading: Sign
steps.text: Apply and sign the membership agreement at enrollment.lfx.linuxfoundation.org/?project=x402-foundation

steps.heading: Onboard
steps.text: Get your Governing/General Board or working-group seat activated; join the public meeting calendar and Slack workspace

steps.heading: Integrate
steps.text: Ship a first integration with the existing SDKs — npm install @x402/core, pip install x402, or go get github.com/x402-foundation/x402/go/v2

steps.heading: Show up
steps.text: Bring your first proposal, question, or use case to a working group — General Members already voting on the Card Acceptance group's direction

slides.text: Sign up now as a member and take a seat at the table shaping how the internet pays.
